component.name: Neversnooze CE
component.summary: Memory scanner, debugger, and injector for modding games and apps

description.p: A Linux-native memory scanner, debugger and code injection toolkit in C++ and Qt6: memory scanning, pointer scanning, an auto-assembler, an interactive multi-thread debugger, structure dissection, cheat tables, and Lua scripting.
Focused on single-player game modding and reverse engineering. It does not target multiplayer anti-cheat.
Based on cheat-engine-linux by wleeaf, inspired by Cheat Engine by Dark Byte.

Ten new reverse-engineering workflows: symbols-first addressing with a searchable symbol browser (records that survive updates by name), a pattern editor with bounded AOB scans and Lua/C export, pattern-resolver records that rebase tables across game updates, a value provenance timeline for find-what-writes, game profiles that auto-attach with a table when a watched game starts, a behavior-driven hunt wizard, table verification before sharing, a guided tour of the core workflows, an overlay HUD with pinned live values, and a memory heatmap of write activity over time.

Neversnooze CE: the engine rebranded as a Neversnooze project with the Neversnooze logo, periwinkle accent theme, new application id and desktop integration, and .rpm packages alongside the .deb and AppImage.
Compatibility work across native, Wine and Proton, ARM64, ARM32, x32, RISC-V, s390x and PowerPC guests, .NET, Mono and emulator targets, with explicit errors where a feature is not supported.
Site-specific auto-assembler injection templates, consistent typed memory operations across the GUI, CLI, and Lua, and extensive correctness fixes for scanning, debugging, parsing, and scripting.
Improved GUI layouts, light and dark themes, scrolling, process selection, live settings, and large form canvases.
Correctness, safety and portability fixes.
Global symbols, code pages and broader Lua support.
Emulator and sandboxed targets, obfuscated values, and scriptable find what writes.
Find what writes and code injection on Wine and Proton.
Whole-application interface overhaul and a deeper IL2CPP dissector.
Scanner performance overhaul.
Mono and Unity dissector, diagnostics, Lua table compatibility and debugger polish.
Bug-fix release: theme, diagnostics and packaging fixes.
Full CLI / headless parity through the Lua API and the cescan runner.
Complete interactive debugger; cecore as a ceserver; untrusted cheat-table security hardening.
AOB-injection fix, 32-bit/WoW64/Wine support, cheat-table inline editing.
Real-time results and a hardened core.
PortProton, Lutris and Heroic support.
First tagged release.
